title: Government Ministers and MPs Targeted by Alleged Misinformation
author: YTS News
summary: Concerns over unverified online accusations against Vanuatu public officials highlight the need for evidence, responsible reporting and the right to scrutinise government.
body: PORT VILA, 23 NOVEMBER 2026 — The circulation of unverified allegations and potentially misleading information on social media involving government ministers, Members of Parliament, diplomats and other public officials has raised questions about reputational harm and responsible online publishing in Vanuatu.

Facebook and other online platforms allow allegations to spread rapidly, sometimes before their accuracy can be established. Public officials are entitled to protection against defamatory statements, but their positions also require them to accept legitimate criticism, scrutiny and accountability.

An allegation is not necessarily false because the person concerned denies it. Equally, a claim is not proven merely because it has been widely shared online. Evidence, attribution and an opportunity to respond are essential when reporting serious accusations.

In Vanuatu's closely connected communities, reputational disputes may also affect families, customary relationships and public trust. This makes careful verification particularly important for social media users, page administrators and news publishers.

Genuine allegations of corruption, misconduct or abuse of office should be assessed independently by the appropriate authorities. Deliberately fabricated allegations, where established, should be addressed through lawful processes that respect freedom of expression and due process.
The central question is not whether government ministers and MPs should face public scrutiny, but whether accusations presented as facts are supported by credible evidence.

YTS News encourages responsible public debate, verification of serious claims and the correction of inaccurate information. This report discusses a general concern; it does not establish that any particular person or organisation has conducted a coordinated misinformation campaign.

title: Welcome to YTS News
author: YTS News Editorial
summary: Introducing a digital newsroom for Vanuatu, built to make public-interest reporting easier to find and read.
body: Welcome to YTS News, a new digital publishing home for stories from across Vanuatu.
Our mission is to provide accessible reporting on government, Parliament, community affairs, business and other matters of public interest.
We aim to verify factual claims, identify sources clearly, correct errors promptly and seek responses from people who are the subject of serious allegations.
This is an introductory announcement for the platform. It is not a report about a current event.
